subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion + HW refresh (A100 → H100 / L40S)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Peter Belmont <peter.belmont@arkedge.ai>, ArkEdge Procurement <procurement@arkedge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion: Dedicated pool expansion + hardware refresh options

Hi Peter / ArkEdge procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call last week — excited to be continuing the partnership. Your renewal window is coming up and I wanted to outline options we can put into the renewal contract so you can make a decision that matches cost and performance goals.

Key asks from your side (as I understood): +32 GPUs of additional reserved capacity, ability to handle burst traffic for new batch workloads, and a hardware refresh from your existing A100 pool to something faster (H100 and L40S were mentioned).

Attached is an initial options packet (RI_dedicated_renewal_options_arkedge_v1.pdf) that summarizes three paths we commonly propose:
- Lift-and-shift extension (add 32 A100s to current pool) — lowest migration friction.
- Hybrid refresh (add 32 H100s, keep a subset of A100s for legacy models) — better throughput per GPU, moderate price premium.
- Aggressive refresh (migrate to L40S-enabled instances with INT8 profiles for quantized models) — highest performance-per-dollar for optimized models, requires evals.

What I need from you to finalize a formal renewal: anticipated sustained tokens/sec targets for peak day, any hard 99th-pct latency SLOs you want contractual, and your procurement timeline for PO/signature. If it helps, I can put together a short throughput-per-dollar sheet comparing A100/H100/L40S for your two primary workloads (chat gen and batched embeddings).

Propose a 30-minute sync next Tuesday (2/17) to walk the numbers. Available windows: 10–11am or 2–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0183

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we jump into a new contract:

1) Performance-per-dollar: can you provide concrete numbers (tokens/sec per GPU and $/100M tokens) for A100 vs H100 vs L40S using models similar to our production models (approx 13B chat model and an embeddings model)? We have an internal bar for cost savings of at least 25% on $/token to justify a migration.
2) Throughput guarantees: procurement will want a committed throughput number for the reserved pool and a description of burst capacity (how many concurrent requests you can absorb and what trigger/rate limits apply).
3) Migration risk: if we move inference to a different device class, outline warm-up / cache priming steps (KV warmup) and any model quantization work you expect.

Procurement timeline: we need a signed agreement by March 15 to align with our budget approvals. I'm attaching our current SOW with the anticipated usage pattern — can you include that in your proposal?

Thanks Peter — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short throughput-per-dollar workbook (RI_throughput_per_dollar_calc_arkedge.xlsx) and a summary below. I ran the numbers against a proxy 13B chat model and your embeddings workload with conservative assumptions (mixed-precision fp16 for H100/A100, INT8 quantized profile for L40S where we recommend it).

Summary (high level):
- Baseline (your current fleet): 64 x A100 (fp16) — measured steady-state throughput: ~1.0x baseline. Effective cost: $Y per 100M tokens (see sheet).
- Option 1 (add 32 A100) — immediate capacity increase ~+50% throughput, minimal migration work, minimal P50/P90 change. Unit cost roughly flat.
- Option 2 (add 32 H100) — per-device throughput: ~1.7x–1.9x of A100 for chat gen (fp16), conservatively 1.6x for embeddings batch paths. After factoring rental/pricing uplift, net improvement in $/100M tokens: ~20–35% savings depending on workload mix.
- Option 3 (transition 50%+ to L40S with INT8 profiles) — for embeddings and quantization-friendly chat prompts, measured throughput can be 2.0x–2.5x of A100; however this requires model quantization validation (we can do evals as part of the migration). Net $/token savings in favorable cases: 30–45%.

Concrete example (illustrative):
- Current monthly committed spend (A100 pool): $240,000 for 64 GPUs (committed rate).
- Add 32 H100s (hybrid pool): incremental committed spend +$150,000/month, but estimated throughput uplift reduces effective $/token such that total cost per expected token volume drops ~22% vs add-A100 path.
- Add 32 L40S and convert 50% of chat inference to INT8: incremental spend +$180,000/month, but with larger token savings if quantization is applicable (we'd need a short eval to confirm).

Operational notes and risk items:
- KV cache warm-up: transitioning model instances to a different hardware class does not preserve runtime KV caches — we recommend a staged rollout with pre-warming traffic (we can orchestrate warmup scripts; estimated 12–48 hours for 95% hit-rate depending on prompt variety).
- Autoscale/burst behavior: dedicated pools can be configured with burst credit. We can commit to a reserved baseline throughput (e.g., X concurrent sessions or Y tokens/sec) and an enforced burst ceiling with SLA-tiered fallback to hosted instances if peak exceeds pool capacity.
- QA/quantization: L40S INT8 requires an eval pass to validate quality. We include one eval run (up to 2k prompts) in the migration package; further tuning is billable.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll produce a formal redlined renewal including 12-month committed pricing for three options (Add-A100, Hybrid H100, L40S-quantized path).
2) We schedule a technical sync with Jonas (runtime) and Rishi (solutions) to validate warm-up and SLO language — how does Tue 2/24 11am PT look?
3) If procurement is on the March 15 timeline, we’ll aim to finalize commercial terms by 3/8 to leave room for PO processing.

I’ve attached the workbook with the numbers used above. If you want, I can also produce a short one-page economic summary for your CFO.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
